reviews.title: Get your weight and nutrition under control
reviews.text:
I've used Lose It and My Fitness Pal, and My Net Diary Pro is the best. It's quick and easy to use. Most every food you will encounter is in here. If it isn't, it's easy to add and link barcodes. 

I recommend using this tool to get your food intake under control. Visually seeing how many calories you have left at the end of the day is huge. If your under, go ahead and have a cookie!  If you're over, go to the gym and burn off that extra 300 calories. 

More than calories, you can also track your intake of Saturated Fat, Sodium and vital nutrients. One feature request, I would like to see them add the ability to track Soluable Fiber and Mono & Polyunsaturated Fat as these are critical to maintaining healthy levels of good/bad cholesterol. 

After a few weeks, you will have created new eating habits and have more energy. Paired with exercise you will be losing weight and feeling great. 

It's EASY. Calories Out > Calories In. This tool keeps you honest!

reviews.title: Nutrition tracker
reviews.text:
This attractive app makes it easy to keep an accurate food diary, and guide my eating – for example, get enough protein, limit calories, and analyze food sensitivities. 

It helpfully lists food suggestions for each meal, based on my past choices; for example my breakfasts are basically the same, with minor variations, and it lets me choose items by just clicking on suggested listed suggestions. It also lets me copy any previous day’s entire meal with just a single swipe. It also has a good search feature, asking me to click on one in a list of food candidates, as you’d expect. Their food library seems quite extensive and useful: the entries all have extensive nutritional details. There are no useless “name only” entries, unlike other apps where users can enter information into the library, even with missing or  incomplete details. 

I’d give it 5 stars if the search feature was more tolerant of misspellings. All said, it’s really easy to use, attractive, and very informative.
.
